messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a ~60% drop in token-level latency metrics for route /generate on inference-04 right after we rolled kernel-selector v2 this morning. dashboard: https://redwood.prod/d/latency-token?panelId=7

oliver: Can you paste the raw StatsD lines? Could be exporter sampling/normalization change rather than real regression.

maria: here's one of the lines captured around the window:
```
statsd: timer tokens.latency:1234|ms|#route:/generate,model:gpt-rw-7b,host:inference-04,seq_len_bucket:0-16
```

jess: I also noticed OTLP spans for kv.cache.hits are much lower for the same hosts. Might be correlated — KV cache telemetry seems suppressed.

kevin: Quick theory: the kernel-selector change toggled a flag that removed the `seq_len_bucket` tag on internal timers. Our StatsD exporter de-duplicates based on tagset, so losing a low-card tag can either aggregate or drop depending on the path. Also saw a line in exporter logs about "high-cardinality metric - dropped" earlier.

oliver: Do we have logs? I saw a few logs from this morning with marshalling errors.

maria: log snippet:
```
2026-04-01T09:12:03Z ERROR statsd-exporter marshalling metric failed: cardinality exceeded limit=50000 metric=tokens.latency tags=...
2026-04-01T09:12:03Z WARN exporter sampling enabled for metric=tokens.latency due to high-card
```

dave: If exporter is sampling aggressively we could see an apparent drop in token-level coverage without any change in actual latency. Two parallel actions: (1) short-term rollback of tag changes in kernel-selector or re-enable seq_len_bucket; (2) backfill token-level metrics from traces/tracing index.

jess: I can run a backfill over the last 6 hours on traces if we want to reconstruct per-token latencies per-route. Command I used previously:
```
./infra/run_backfill --index traces-prod --from 1804497600 --to 1804501200 --query 'route:/generate AND span.name:token' --out s3://redwood-backfill/180450-backfill.jsonl
```
Note: this will rebuild metrics from spans, not from StatsD — any samples never emitted won't be recoverable.

kevin: Also note that some KV cache events were being emitted with dynamic keys (model+shard) which ballooned cardinality after the kernel flags changed prefetch behavior. Need a normalization pass in the runtime before we emit tags.

oliver: Agreed on long-term fixes: add unit test for kernel-selector to assert metric tag set invariants; add a regression alert that fires when token-level metric coverage for a route drops >40% in a 5m window.

maria: For immediate mitigation I'll open a PR to re-enable `seq_len_bucket` tagging in the kernel path and add a temporary exporter config to aggregate token latency by `route,model` only. Will post link.

jess: Backfill job started (job id bf-2026-04-01-09-30). I'll stream progress here. :rocket:

sre-bot: scheduled reingest job id reingest-2026-04-01-09-34 for s3://metrics-raw/18045/ with priority=high

maria: Thanks team. Action items: maria -> PR for tag normalization, oliver -> alert rule, jess -> backfill progress, kevin -> runtime normalization RFC, dave -> oncall follow-up. @dave please take ownership for postmortem if backfill shows data loss.

dave: Taking it. Will coordinate with infra to reingest exporter payloads and validate dashboards once backfill completes.

maria: 👍 closing the loop once job finishes, will attach perf profile comparisons (before/after kernel switch) to the RFC.
